A geometric LLN/CLT yields the condensed tilted-uniform law and current; the local geometric CLT plus exponential lower-tail bounds yield the critical 2D density and current. Uniform-integrability and all boundary cases are addressed; the standalone 28 finite-state cases independently check balance, canonical probabilities and current, while larger tests check convergence. Finite experiments are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: This natural two-bottleneck particle-transport model has a motivated competing-condensate selection problem. The same physical vanishing rate asymmetry is detectable at order 1/sqrt(L) at critical density but order 1/L in the extensive condensed regime. The joint limiting laws, scaling-sensitive bias, and explicit first stationary current corrections quantify a nontrivial finite-size crossover beyond simply restating factorized steady states. It is a narrow but structurally interpretable exact result.
